questions.knowledge_point: Identifying Linearly Independent and Dependent Sets Using Row Reduction
questions.problem:
Consider the following vectors:

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 3 \\ -4\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 10 \\ -12\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 8 \\ -16\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Assume that ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},$ and ${x}_{3}$ are real numbers. Which of the following statements are true?

- The equation ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=0$ has only the trivial solution ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=0.$
- The vectors ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},$ and ${a}_{3}$ are linearly dependent.
- The vectors ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},$ and ${a}_{3}$ are linearly independent.
questions.worked_solution:
We say that three vectors ${v}_{1},{v}_{2},$ and ${v}_{3}$ are *linearly independent* if the only solution to the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{2}{v}_{2}+{x}_{3}{v}_{3}=0
$$

is ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=0.$ Otherwise, the vectors are *linearly dependent*.

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

The equation ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=0$ corresponds to the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}_{1}+3{x}_{2}+4{x}_{3}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}+10{x}_{2}+8{x}_{3}=0 \\ -4{x}_{1}-12{x}_{2}-16{x}_{3}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system, we create its augmented matrix and reduce it using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 4 & 0 \\ 3 & 10 & 8 & 0 \\ -4 & -12 & -16 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-3){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & 0 \\ -4 & -12 & -16 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+4{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we conclude that the basic variables are ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$, while ${x}_{3}$ is the free variable. 

Since there is one free variable, the equation ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=0$ has an infinite number of nonzero solutions, which means that the vectors are linearly dependent. 

Therefore, statements I and III are false, while statement II is true.

questions.problem:
Consider the following vectors:

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 4 \\ -2\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ 15 \\ -7\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -4 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$

 

Assume that ${x}_{1},{x}_{2},$ and ${x}_{3}$ are real numbers. Which of the following statements are true?

- The equation ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=0$  has an infinite number of nonzero solutions.
- The vectors ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},$ and ${a}_{3}$ are linearly dependent.
- The vectors ${a}_{1},{a}_{2},$ and ${a}_{3}$ are linearly independent.
questions.worked_solution:
We say that three vectors ${v}_{1},{v}_{2},$ and ${v}_{3}$ are *linearly independent* if the only solution to the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{2}{v}_{2}+{x}_{3}{v}_{3}=0
$$

is ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=0.$ Otherwise, the vectors are *linearly dependent*.

With that in mind, let's examine our statements.

The equation ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=0$ corresponds to the system 

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+7{x}_{2}-{x}_{3}=0 \\ 4{x}_{1}+15{x}_{2}-4{x}_{3}=0 \\ -2{x}_{1}-7{x}_{2}+{x}_{3}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

To solve the system, we create its augmented matrix and reduce it using Gaussian elimination:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}2 & 7 & -1 & 0 \\ 4 & 15 & -4 & 0 \\ -2 & -7 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 7 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ -2 & -7 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}2 & 7 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

From the matrix above, we conclude that the basic variables are ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$, while ${x}_{3}$ is the free variable. 

Since there is one free variable, the equation ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=0$ has an infinite number of nonzero solutions, which means that the vectors are linearly dependent. 

Therefore, statement III is false, while statements I and II are true.

questions.knowledge_point: Identifying Linearly Independent Sets by Inspection
questions.problem:
Consider the following vectors:

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}]
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

- ${a}_{1}-2{a}_{2}=0.$
- ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=0$ only if ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=0.$
- The set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is linearly independent.
questions.worked_solution:
We say that two vectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2}$ are *linearly independent* if the only solution to the equation

$$
{x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{2}{v}_{2}=0
$$

is ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=0.$ Otherwise, the vectors are *linearly dependent*.

With that in mind, let's look at each statement in turn.

- Statement I is false. Indeed:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1}-2{a}_{2} & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]-2[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ -2 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & \ne 0\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement II is true. The equation ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=0$ corresponds to the system

$$
{\begin{aligned}2{x}_{1}+{x}_{2}=0 \\ {x}_{2}=0 \\ 3{x}_{1}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system using back substitution, we find that the solution is ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=0.$

- Statement III is true. Since statement II is true, the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2}}$ is linearly independent.

Therefore, the correct answer is "II and III only."

$$

Which of the following statements are true?

- ${a}_{1}-3{a}_{2}+{a}_{3}=0.$
- ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=0$ only if ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=0.$
- The set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is linearly independent.

$$
{x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{2}{v}_{2}+{x}_{3}{v}_{3}=0
$$

is ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}={x}_{3}=0.$ Otherwise, the vectors are *linearly dependent*.

With that in mind, let's look at each statement in turn.

- Statement I is true. Indeed:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1}-3{a}_{2}+{a}_{3} & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]-3[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 4\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 5 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ -6 \\ -12\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 1 \\ 10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-1-3+4 \\ 5-6+1 \\ 2-12+10\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement II is false. Since statement I is true, we have ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}+{x}_{3}{a}_{3}=0$ for ${x}_{1}={x}_{3}=1$ and ${x}_{2}=-3.$

- Statement III is false. Since statement II is false, the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is linearly *dependent*.

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."

$$

$$

- $4{a}_{1}+{a}_{2}=0.$
- ${x}_{1}{a}_{1}+{x}_{2}{a}_{2}=0$ only if ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=0.$

{x}_{1}{v}_{1}+{x}_{2}{v}_{2}=0

$$
\begin{aligned}4{a}_{1}+{a}_{2} & =4[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1 \\ 3\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -4 \\ -12\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-8 \\ 4 \\ 12\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}8 \\ -4 \\ -12\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}] \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$
